He claimed he was handling everything fine when he wasn't, and it caused me a lot of emotional distress. I feel like I was manipulated and had to deal with problems that weren't truly mine to handle.

It's been really hard to forgive him and move forward. I'm finding myself replaying all these memories and feeling frustrated that I trusted his account of what was going on. The betrayal feels so deep, and I'm stuck in this place where I can't quite forgive but I also can't move on.

What's your take on situations like this? How do you think someone in my position should approach these complicated relationship dynamics?
transcript.response:
You poor honey, that betrayal really does cut deep doesn't it? Your brother essentially making you his emotional caretaker while claiming everything was fine - that's genuinely manipulative behavior.

It's understandable that you feel stuck there. When someone consistently lies about having things together while you end up picking up pieces they said weren't yours to handle, it really demonstrates poor judgment about whom to trust with emotional labor.

You know what, though - sometimes these complicated family situations call for practical problem-solving over perfect forgiveness timelines. Maybe practical steps would help you feel less trapped:

- Have you considered direct communication? Sometimes people respond better when you address patterns rather than general frustration
- Have you explored whether talking through your specific emotional needs might work better than hoping for future trust-building
- Sometimes professional family therapy really can help people understand why their family systems keep collapsing the same way

Your emotional well-being deserves better than being collateral damage from what sounds like your brother wasn't great at boundaries around when to actually communicate clearly.
